costRanges.item: Spot reseal of a single transition
Flashing reseal or small flashing section

lifespans.item: Repair-vs-replace age threshold for localized chimney leak

signs: Brown or yellow ceiling stains on the upper floor near the chimney chase (water entering at the chimney flashing, the roof's largest penetration)
Rusted, lifted, or bent step flashing along the chimney sidewall (most common flashing failure mode alongside corrosion and short laps, per GAF)
Counter flashing pulled loose or hanging from the mortar joint (breaks the mechanical lock the NRCA two-part system sets into the reglet)
Cracked caulk or roofing cement smeared along the chimney base (a temporary surface fix failing, per IIBEC)
A continuous one-piece metal strip at the chimney sidewall (a defective installation; step flashing seals only when woven one piece per shingle course, per InterNACHI and shingle manufacturers)
Ice buildup and meltwater backup on the upslope side of a chimney wider than 30 inches (indicates a missing cricket required by IRC R1003.20)

technicalFacts.fact: Correct chimney flashing is a two-part system: base and step flashing woven one piece per shingle course, plus a separate counter (cap) flashing set into a reglet cut in a horizontal mortar joint, overlapping the step flashing.
A continuous one-piece metal strip at a chimney/sidewall is a defective installation; step flashing must be individual pieces woven one per shingle course.

Surface caulk or roofing cement alone over no underlying metal is a temporary fix that cracks within a few years from masonry-versus-roof differential movement and freeze-thaw; a permanent repair rebuilds both metal layers rather than smearing sealant over the symptom.
The counter flashing locks into the masonry mechanically (set into a reglet cut in the mortar joint) rather than relying on adhesive that masonry-versus-roof movement breaks.
A self-adhering polymer-modified ice-and-water membrane applied at the chimney base self-seals around fasteners.

The chimney is the roof's largest penetration, with the downslope apron, the two sidewall step runs, and the upslope head/cricket transitions all needing to shed water — diagnosis traces the failed transition before resealing.
The roofing industry estimates that roughly 90-95% of roof leaks originate at flashing details (only 5-10% at the open shingle field) — keep hedged as an industry estimate attributed to the NRCA.
On a detached one- and two-family dwelling, a repair of the roof covering counts as ordinary maintenance and requires no construction permit, inspection, or notice to the construction official.
On a commercial building, repairing more than 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period requires a permit; a localized chimney flashing repair stays within the ordinary-maintenance threshold.

codes.requirement: A cricket/saddle is required on the upslope side of a chimney wider than 30 inches measured parallel to the ridge (that does not intersect the ridge); the cricket diverts water, ice, and snow around the chimney.
Self-adhering polymer-modified bitumen ice-and-water membrane that self-seals around fasteners — applied at the chimney base.
Roof-covering repair on a detached one/two-family dwelling is ordinary maintenance (no permit); on a commercial building, repairing >25% of total roof area in 12 months requires a permit.

defabToKill.issue: Claims chimney flashing failures 'cause more roof leaks in Essex County homes than any other single component' / 'the most common cause of persistent roof leaks' — an unsourced absolute.
defabToKill.fix: Use the hedged framing: the chimney is the roof's largest penetration and the roofing industry estimates roughly 90-95% of roof leaks originate at flashing details, an industry estimate attributed to the NRCA. Do not claim chimney flashing is THE most common single leak cause.

defabToKill.issue: Implies ice dams are simply a chimney-leak driver without acknowledging root cause; risks treating ice-dam pressure as a flashing problem.
defabToKill.fix: Per §0, ice-dam root cause = attic heat loss / air leakage (Building Science Digest 135 / Univ. of Minnesota Extension); ice-dam meltwater can back up past base flashing on the upslope chimney face, but do not attribute ice dams to flashing or gutters.

defabToKill.issue: Specifies 'high-quality urethane sealant' as the correct seal — overstates sealant's role and contradicts the gold's IIBEC point.
defabToKill.fix: Counter flashing must be mechanically locked into a reglet cut in the mortar joint per the NRCA two-part standard; sealant alone over no underlying metal is a temporary fix that cracks within a few years, per IIBEC.

defabToKill.issue: 'NJ building code requires a cricket on chimneys wider than 30 inches' — vague code citation.
defabToKill.fix: Cite IRC Section R1003.20: a cricket/saddle is required on the upslope side of a chimney wider than 30 inches measured parallel to the ridge.

defabToKill.issue: 'chimney leaks escalate rapidly in NJ homes over 25 years old' — invented age-specific escalation claim with no source.
defabToKill.fix: Drop the invented 25-year figure; keep the qualitative point that mortar joint deterioration and flashing aging compromise the seal together. Repair-vs-replace age threshold in the gold is 'roof under 10-15 years' (contractor consensus).

defabToKill.issue: Invented cost ranges not in the gold: full chimney flashing replacement '$800 to $2,500'; cricket install '$500-1,500'; repointing '$300-800'; full repointing '$1,000-3,000'; crown repair '$300-800'.
defabToKill.fix: Use ONLY the named-source ranges in the gold: chimney flashing repair $300-$1,800 (most $400-$1,600), spot reseal $150-$300 (HomeGuide/Angi), flashing reseal/small section $200-$500 (Modernize). Cricket and reglet add labor cost (no invented dollar amount) — frame qualitatively + free written estimate.

defabToKill.issue: Invented deferred-damage total: 'a $1,500 flashing repair deferred by two years typically results in $3,000-8,000 in interior damage' — fabricated whole-project total with no named aggregator.
defabToKill.fix: Remove the fabricated $3,000-$8,000 interior-damage total; the gold has NO whole-project total. State qualitatively that deferral risks interior damage and frame against the named per-repair ranges + free estimate.

defabToKill.issue: '$200-500' re-sealing range presented as Essex County market data without naming a source, and conflated with surface caulk reseal.
defabToKill.fix: The $200-$500 figure is Modernize flashing-section data; the spot reseal of a single transition is $150-$300 per HomeGuide/Angi. Attribute each range to its named source.

defabToKill.issue: 'NJ insurance policies increasingly exclude gradual water damage' — unsourced insurance generalization.
defabToKill.fix: Drop the unsourced insurance claim or hedge it; keep focus on the named cost ranges and the value of timely repair via free written estimate.

defabToKill.issue: 'differential movement... is the primary cause of chimney flashing failure' stated as fact, then 'amplified by Essex County's 80+ annual freeze-thaw cycles' — the 80+ freeze-thaw figure is invented/unsourced.
defabToKill.fix: Keep differential movement + freeze-thaw as a qualitative failure driver (per IIBEC); remove the invented '80+ annual freeze-thaw cycles' number. Newark/Essex = IRC Climate Zone 4-5.

defabToKill.issue: 'galvanic corrosion between dissimilar metals (copper flashing against aluminum drip edge)' presented as a common secondary cause — not supported by the gold.
defabToKill.fix: Drop or de-emphasize; the gold's failure modes are corrosion/rust, lifted/bent by wind, short laps, and sealant cracking (GAF/IIBEC). Do not invent galvanic-pair specifics.

defabToKill.issue: 'A comprehensive chimney flashing replacement during a re-roof costs 40-60% less than standalone chimney work' — invented percentage with no named source.
defabToKill.fix: Remove the fabricated 40-60% figure; the gold has no such statistic. State qualitatively that combining the work with a reroof avoids duplicate shingle removal.

defabToKill.issue: Repair-vs-replace thresholds ('less than 15 years', 'older than 20 years') differ from the gold's stated thresholds.
defabToKill.fix: Align to the gold FAQ: repair when the leak stays localized at the chimney transitions on a roof under 10-15 years old; replace the roof when damage exceeds 25-30% of roof area or one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost (contractor-consensus thresholds).

defabToKill.issue: References 'NJ code requires crickets on chimneys wider than 30 inches' vaguely.
defabToKill.fix: Cite IRC Section R1003.20 with the 'measured parallel to the ridge' qualifier.

articleAngles.signs: Definitively answer that chimney flashing needs repair when you see specific symptoms — brown/yellow ceiling stains on the upper floor near the chimney, rusted/lifted/bent step flashing, counter flashing pulled from the mortar joint, cracked caulk along the base, a tell-tale continuous one-piece strip (defective install), or ice/meltwater backup on the upslope side of a chimney wider than 30 inches. Strongest grounded facts: chimney = roof's largest penetration + hedged 90-95% NRCA flashing-leak estimate; GAF failure modes (corrosion/lifted/short-lap); InterNACHI one-piece-strip = defective; IIBEC sealant-cracks-in-a-few-years; IRC R1003.20 missing-cricket symptom.
articleAngles.costGuide: Definitively answer the cost using ONLY named-source ranges: chimney flashing repair runs $300-$1,800, with most repairs $400-$1,600 and a spot reseal of a single transition $150-$300 (HomeGuide and Angi); a flashing reseal or small flashing section runs $200-$500 (Modernize). A cricket (IRC R1003.20, chimney >30 in) and a counter-flashing reglet cut add labor over a surface reseal (frame qualitatively, no invented dollar add-ons); close with Newark Quality Roofing's free written estimate. No whole-project total exists in the gold — do not fabricate one.
articleAngles.decision: Broad homeowner overview: explain that correct chimney flashing is the NRCA two-part system (base/step flashing woven one piece per shingle course + separate counter flashing set into a reglet cut in a mortar joint), that a continuous one-piece strip is a defective install (InterNACHI/shingle mfrs), that sealant alone is a temporary fix cracking within a few years from masonry-vs-roof movement and freeze-thaw (IIBEC), that a cricket is code-required on chimneys >30 in parallel to the ridge (IRC R1003.20), and a self-adhering ice-and-water membrane at the base self-seals around fasteners (ASTM D1970). Repair when localized on a roof under 10-15 yrs; replace the roof at >25-30% area damage or when one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost. Verify the contractor rebuilds both metal layers rather than caulking, and note NJ permit framing (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7: roof-covering repair = ordinary maintenance on a 1-2 family home).
